speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned persistent vomiting and chest pain; to begin my assessment, have you experienced any difficulty breathing or fainting, and when did these symptoms first start?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (spontaneous esophageal rupture).

I have confirmed the clinical picture of forceful retching following heavy alcohol consumption, leading to sudden chest pain and choking. The combination of these specific events and symptoms is highly characteristic of an esophageal tear. Do you have any difficulty swallowing or are you producing saliva that you cannot swallow due to the pain?
